sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Sunderland's recent policy is mostly about prices. A statutory notice published in the Sunderland Echo on 8 May 2026 said the council would vary parking charges, with the notice coming into force on 1 June 2026: surface car park rates rise by 20p an hour, for example from 1.40 to 1.60 pounds at Boughton Street and from 1.10 to 1.30 at Charles Street, and where an all-day rate is listed it goes from 5.00 to 5.50 pounds, with the Sunday and bank holiday rate rising from 3.00 to 3.50 pounds [0]. Station Car Park on Holmeside rises from 1.50 to 1.70 pounds an hour and from 7.00 to 7.50 a day, with Monday to Friday 3pm to midnight staying free, and on-street pay bays in the centre also rise [1][2]. We read the notice only, not a council page, so we cannot confirm the charges are being applied. The council's own site is bot-protected and we did not open it; we found no resident-parking scheme or parking strategy.

The stated policy aim, when the contractor for the Farringdon Row car park was appointed in 2021, was to put modern parking at the edge of the city so people drive to Sunderland, not through it [5].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The council approved a programme of about 2 million pounds in May 2025 for maintenance and upgrades at its St Mary's and Sunniside multi-storey car parks, covering facades, solar panels, lighting, CCTV and cycle storage; a contractor was still to be appointed [6]. The Farringdon Row car park in Riverside Sunderland was described in 2021 as 650 spaces with 15 percent electric-vehicle spaces [5]; a council headline from June 2023 reports its opening, but we could not open the page and do not state its size or opening as confirmed [3]. The Riverside masterplan aims to double the city-centre resident population from 2,500 to 5,000, which adds to expected demand around it, although the article does not mention parking [7]. Planning permission was granted in October 2022 for a 404-space multi-storey car park on a derelict Holmeside site, with 92 EV charging bays; we do not know whether it was built as approved [10]. At St Mary's four 7kW chargers were due to be operational in April 2022 [11]. Paid parking was announced for the Stadium of Light car parks from 26 August 2025, free for under two hours and 10 pounds for 24 hours, in a notice published by a school based at the stadium [8].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The council's open dataset 'Sunderland Car Parks' lists 48 public car parks with space counts but was last updated in August 2013 and has no live occupancy [12]. The Tyne and Wear traffic unit says it provides quarterly average occupancy for each Metro park-and-ride car park, but the page we read contains no figures [13]. We could not source the private and multi-storey operators.

Our data cover one car park, the Stadium of Light Metro park-and-ride with 182 spaces, from the Tyne and Wear feed, measured since 25 September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 17% on weekdays and 7% at weekends, and reached full in a single Saturday-lunchtime reading, which suggests a match-day or event pattern. This says little about the city centre's own car parks, where we have no live data.
